'''''Leucanthemum ircutianum''''' is a [[Herbaceous plant|herbaceous]] [[Perennial plant|perennial]] plant species in the family [[Asteraceae]],<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Navadna ivanjščica - Urbanatura|url=https://www.urbanatura.si/vsebina/499/Navadna-ivanjscica|access-date=2021-09-05|website=www.urbanatura.si|language=sl}}</ref> that can be found growing in [[Eurasia]]n (mostly European) countries and North America.<ref name=":2" /> Just like the similar ''[[Leucanthemum vulgare|L. vulgare]]'', it is commonly known as the '''oxeye daisy'''.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leucanthemum ircutianum DC., Oxeye daisy (Provence, France)|url=https://identify.plantnet.org/provence/species/Leucanthemum%2520ircutianum%2520DC./data|access-date=2021-09-05|website=Pl@ntNet|language=en}}</ref>

== Taxonomy ==
Species name and the first formal description were given to this plant by Swiss botanist [[Augustin Pyramus de Candolle]] in year 1838.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Leucanthemum ircutianum (Turcz.) DC.|url=https://www.gbif.org/species/5401008|access-date=2021-09-05|website=www.gbif.org|language=en}}</ref>

Even though taxonomy of this species and related taxa is complicated,<ref name=":0" /> there are currently three recognized [[subspecies]]:<ref name=":2" />

* ''Leucanthemum ircutianum'' subsp. ''asperulum'' (N.Terracc.) Vogt & Greuter
* ''Leucanthemum ircutianum'' subsp. ''ircutianum''
* ''Leucanthemum ircutianum'' subsp. ''leucolepis'' ([[Briq.]] & Cavill.) Vogt & Greuter
Some authors list additional two subspecies:<ref name=":4" />

* ''Leucanthemum ircutianum'' subsp. ''cantabricum'' (Sennen) Vogt
* ''Leucanthemum ircutianum'' subsp. ''crassifolium'' (Lange) Vogt

== Description ==
This upright-growing herbaceous perennial daisy can reach from 20 to 80 centimetres of height. Its stem is usually firm, covered with short [[trichome]]s and only rarely spread out. Alternately arranged leaves are simple, they are sessile (without leafstalk) and serrated or shallowly lobed, while being [[lanceolate]] to [[spatulate]] in shape.<ref name=":0" /> There are no [[stipule]]s.<ref name=":5">[https://pladias.cz/en/taxon/data/Leucanthemum%20ircutianum Data: ''Leucanthemum ircutianum''] Pladias – Database of the Czech Flora and Vegetation. www.pladias.cz. Retrieved 5. September 2021.</ref>

Like other species of the family [[Asteraceae]], ''L. ircutianum'' has flowers united into so-called [[pseudanthium]] (calathidium), with outer layer consisting of multiple whiteish strap-shaped [[ray flowers]] and inner area being of numerous yellowish circular-shaped tiny [[disc flowers]]. [[Bract]]s are present; the inflorescence is surrounded with lanceolate [[involucral]] leaves. Calyx is modified into a [[Pappus (botany)|pappus]].<ref name=":0" />

This species [[Ovary (botany)|ovary]] is inferior. Seed is enclosed into a brown dry fruit that is called an [[achene]] (more specifically [[Cypsela (botany)|cypsela]]).<ref name=":0" /><ref name=":5" /> ''L. ircutianum'' is an [[entomophilous]] species, that attracts various insect pollinators with its big and noticeable inflorescences that imitate a single flower.<ref name=":0" /> This daisy flowers between May and October.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Leucanthemum ircutianum (navadna ivanjščica)|url=http://www.botanicni-vrt.si/component/rastline/leucanthemum-ircutianum|access-date=2021-09-05|website=www.botanicni-vrt.si|language=sl}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Leucanthemum ircutianum|url=https://sloveniahiking.rocks/en/flowers/leucanthemumircutianum/|access-date=2021-09-05|website=sloveniahiking.rocks}}</ref>

=== Similar species ===
Species ''L. ircutianum'' is very similar to ''[[Leucanthemum vulgare|L. vulgare]]''. Besides some morphological (such as size, [[pollen]]) and ecological differences (eg. flowering time, type of habitats), species also differ in their [[genome]], with ''L. ircutianum'' being [[tetraploid]] and ''L. vulgare'' exhibiting [[diploidy]]. They have mostly similar distribution area in Europe, but ''L. vulgare'' is more common in North America.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Leucanthemum vulgare (oxeye daisy)|url=https://www.cabi.org/isc/datasheet/13357|access-date=2021-09-05|website=www.cabi.org|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=Bährle-Rapp|first=Marina|chapter=Chrysanthemum leucanthemum|date=2007|chapter-url=http://dx.doi.org/10.1007/978-3-540-71095-0_1947|title=Springer Lexikon Kosmetik und Körperpflege|pages=106|place=Berlin, Heidelberg|publisher=Springer Berlin Heidelberg|doi=10.1007/978-3-540-71095-0_1947 |isbn=978-3-540-71094-3 |access-date=2021-09-05|chapter-url-access=subscription}}</ref> In Canada, where both daisies can be found growing, ''L. ircutianum'' occurs primarily in the east parts of the country.<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":3">{{Cite journal|last1=Clements|first1=David R.|last2=Cole|first2=Dan E.|last3=King|first3=Jane|last4=McClay|first4=Alec|date=2004-01-01|title=The biology of Canadian weeds. 128. Leucanthemum vulgare Lam.|journal=Canadian Journal of Plant Science|volume=84|issue=1|pages=343–363|doi=10.4141/p02-112|issn=0008-4220|doi-access=}}</ref>

== Distribution and habitat ==
The oxeye daisy is a plant of Eurasia (mostly Europe, with some parts of Asia) and North America.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=Leucanthemum ircutianum DC. {{!}} Plants of the World Online {{!}} Kew Science|url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/urn:lsid:ipni.org:names:230023-1|access-date=2021-09-05|website=Plants of the World Online|language=en}}</ref> European countries that fall into species' distribution area are Germany, France, former Soviet Union, Spain and Italy,<ref name=":2" /> as well as Albania, Austria, Baltic States, Belgium, Bulgaria, Finland, Great Britain, Portugal, Romania, Sardinia, Sicily, Sweden, Switzerland and former Yugoslavian countries.<ref name=":4" /> In America ''L. ircutianum'' can be found in both USA and eastern parts of Canada.<ref name=":2" /><ref name=":3" />

This daisy flower usually grows in various habitats, including some anthropologically modified [[urban area]]s. Commonly the species can be found on different meadows, forest edges, near paths and roads, as well as in various other [[Ruderal species|ruderal]] landscapes.<ref name=":0" />

The [[Raunkiær system]] classifies it as a [[hemicryptophyte]] species.<ref name=":5" />
